stories.author: Judd Legum
stories.title: McConnell, out sick for two months, voted against medical leave 23 times since 1985
stories.text: Senator Mitch McConnell (R-KY) in July 2026. (Office of Senator Mitch McConnell) Senator Mitch McConnell (R-KY) was hospitalized on June 14 after suffering a fall that left him unconscious. He remained hospitalized until mid-July, when he was transferred to a rehabilitation center . On August 6, McConnell announced that he was discharged and was continuing his recovery at home . But, two months later, McConnell has not returned to work in the Senate. Over that period of time, he has missed 59 floor votes . Nevertheless, McConnell has continued to receive his Senate salary of $174,000 per year . McConnell is fortunate to be employed in a job with excellent benefits. There is no federal law, however, that provides guaranteed paid sick leave. In 2025, about 27 million private sector workers had no paid sick leave. One reason: Mitch McConnell. Since he entered the Senate in 1985, McConnell has voted against creating or expanding medical leave — paid and unpaid — at least 23 times. Notably, near the beginning of his tenure, McConnell supported the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA), which provided up to 12 weeks of unpaid medical leave to care for yourself, a child, a spouse, or a pare

stories.author: The Lever team
stories.title: Meet The Billionaire Behind Connecticut’s “Insurgent” Victory
stories.text: When 14-term Connecticut Rep. John Larson lost his Democratic primary to 47-year-old former Hartford Mayor Luke Bronin yesterday, The New York Times framed it as an insurgent upstart “capitalizing on calls for generational change in the party.” But the money trails behind the race tell a different story. As The Lever revealed in a new investigation, Bronin is deeply tied to 70-year-old billionaire hedge fund manager Stephen Mandel, a longtime Democratic donor who’s become the largest bankroller of a nascent political machine promising to “redefine” the Democratic Party — by moving it back to the more “ moderate” middle . Bronin has the support of the Bench, which, along with Majority Democrats, forms a new Mandel-backed “party within a party” bankrolling a slate of chosen candidates, often with more “moderate” (read: corporate) sensibilities. Mandel and his wife, who live in Connecticut, have given more than $15 million in support to these groups so far this primary season, part of $24 million they’ve donated in total. Bronin also used to be on the payroll of a nonprofit funded by Mandel — and has taken positions on charter schools and artificial intelligence that align with Mandel

stories.author: Drop Site team
stories.title: In West Bank Village, a New Israeli Order Enables Settler Attacks While Claiming to Prevent Them
stories.text: TAYBEH, Occupied West Bank*—On Sunday, the Israeli military declared the Palestinian village of Taybeh in the occupied West Bank a closed military zone, claiming the order was aimed to prevent escalating attacks by marauding Israeli settlers. It ostensibly bars Israelis and foreigners from entering the area. But residents of the village and the surrounding area told Drop Site News that the military order is designed to further isolate Taybeh from the outside world, barring solidarity activists from the area while allowing settler attacks to continue. One of the few Christian-majority Palestinian villages in the West Bank, Taybeh has come under growing attacks by Israeli settlers who have expanded colonial outposts encircling it over the past several weeks. “The order says that Israelis and foreigners are prohibited from entering the area. What about the settler roaming around the area? What is he? Is he Israeli or not? Why is he in the area?,” said Jack Abed, the priest of the Greek Catholic Church in Taybeh. “This order is intended to prevent human rights defenders from being present to defend us against what these settler thugs are doing—attacking us in an extremely brutal manner
